title: Tokyo

description.main: Takashi Homma's first book for an international audience, published by Aperture in 2008, selects from six earlier Japanese titles on Tokyo including Tokyo Suburbia. Essay by Ivan Vartanian; paperback, 239 pages, about 125 colour plates.
description.extended:
Takashi Homma's first book for an international audience, a 2008 Aperture survey of the Tokyo photographs that made his name, drawn from six earlier Japanese titles including Tokyo Suburbia.

The book gathers more than a decade of work on the capital and its edges: housing estates and chain restaurants, highways and car parks, rooftop gardens, teenagers and small children, and the sea and mountains at the city's margin. Homma works in flat, even colour at a measured distance. The cover is My dog, Royce 1, 2005, one of the later pictures in which he turns toward his own studio and household. An essay by Ivan Vartanian places the work within contemporary Japanese photography. Designed by de.MO, it is a 239-page paperback at 7 by 10 inches with about 125 colour plates.

Takashi Homma (b. 1962, Tokyo) left Nihon University in 1984 for agency work, worked for i-D in London in 1991 and 1992, and received the Kimura Ihei Award in 1999 for Tokyo Suburbia. Later books include Trails and The Narcissistic City (MACK) and Portrait of J (Dashwood Books and Session Press, 2025). The library also holds his Portrait, Scandinavian Mushroom and Portrait of J.
description.artist_bio: Takashi Homma (b. 1962, Tokyo) studied photography at Nihon University College of Art, left in 1984 for an in-house job at a Tokyo advertising agency, and worked for i-D in London in 1991-92. Tokyo Suburbia (Korinsha, 1998) won the Kimura Ihei Award in 1999. Retrospectives at the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa (2010) and Tokyo Photographic Art Museum (Revolution 9, 2023). Later books with MACK (Trails, The Narcissistic City, Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji) and Dashwood/Session (Portrait of J, 2025).

notes: Shelf: Japanese. Published as Takashi Homma: Tokyo; the spine reads TAKASHI HOMMA TOKYO. Page count 239 per the Getty Research Institute and OpenLibrary/LC records (Aperture's store page says 256 pages and credits an introductory essay by Ferdinand Brueggemann; the book's page 5 credits an essay by Ivan Vartanian per the Getty record, which is used here). Paperback with flaps per dealer listings.
